expected.title: Satisfiability of first-order sentences is undecidable
expected.author: The Open Logic Project contributors
expected.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own corollary cor:undecidable-sat at source lines 1537-1539: it is undecidable whether an arbitrary sentence of first-order logic is satisfiable. The proof at source lines 1541-1556 is a reduction that has to be assembled step by step. It assumes a Turing machine S deciding satisfiability and then describes a machine that would decide validity: copy the input sentence, write a negation symbol in front of it, run S on the negated sentence, and translate the answer back, using that a sentence is valid exactly when its negation is unsatisfiable. The description is given at the level of tape operations (moving the sentence one square, returning to square 1, writing the negation, inspecting square 1 for a stroke, erasing or writing one), so the reader has to accept that these are computable operations and that the resulting machine halts on every input. The contradiction is then with the already established unsolvability of the decision problem for validity. Nothing in the statement names the reduction or the two closure facts it uses. No result outside the retained text is used.
